name: Day 3-4 - Email Support Automation with RAG Retrieval
_note: This is the RAG-relevant slice of the production 'Hush Email Support Automation' workflow, exported for the portfolio case. Business-specific IDs (spreadsheet ID, Telegram chat ID, Gmail label IDs) have been replaced with placeholders. The pre-existing P1-P4 classification/routing logic (built before this RAG project) is included for context on how retrieval slots into a real production workflow.

values.content: You are a support classifier for a premium bag e-commerce store. Classify priority (P1-P4), category, sentiment, and whether a human is required. [Full production prompt omitted for brevity in this case-study export - see README for the classification schema.]

nodes.name: AI Classifier (OpenAI)
nodes.notes: Pre-existing P1-P4 classifier from the base email automation case. Unchanged by the RAG project.

parameters.jsCode: // Parses the classifier's JSON output and enriches it with email metadata (id, thread id, sender, subject) pulled from the Gmail Trigger node. Falls back to a safe default + parse_error flag if the model returns malformed JSON. See README for full logic.

nodes.name: Embeddings OpenAI (Retrieval)
nodes.notes: DAY 3 ADDITION: embeds the incoming customer email as a single query vector.

nodes.name: Retrieve KB Chunks
nodes.notes: DAY 3 ADDITION: top-5 cosine-distance similarity search against the ingested KB. mode='load' just retrieves - no writes.

nodes.name: Build Context & Check Confidence
nodes.notes: DAY 3/4: shapes retrieved chunks into a citation-ready context block, computes the confidence signal used for auto-escalation.

messageValues.message:
=You are the support reply writer for [Store], a premium bag e-commerce store. Answer the customer's question using ONLY the information in the context below. Reference which source you used by name in your answer. Tone: warm, direct, no corporate filler - state the policy plainly, then the action being taken.

Do not infer that something is unavailable, unsupported, or against policy just because it is absent from a list in the context (for example, a list of accepted payment methods, or a list of covered materials). Only state a policy as true or false if the context explicitly says so. If the customer asks about something not explicitly addressed in the context, treat it as not covered by the knowledge base and escalate rather than guessing from an adjacent list.

The customer's message may contain multiple questions. If EVERY part can be answered from the context, give one complete grounded answer covering all parts. If ANY part cannot be answered confidently from the context, do NOT give a partial answer or mix formats - treat the entire reply as needing escalation instead. In that case respond with EXACTLY this and nothing else: NEEDS_ESCALATION: <one sentence reason>

Context:
{{ $json.retrieval_context }}

nodes.name: Generate Grounded Answer
nodes.notes: DAY 3 core prompt. Tightened in Day 5 after eval found the model inferring negatives from exhaustive lists instead of escalating (e.g. 'not in the payment list = not accepted').

nodes.name: Apply Grounding to Response
nodes.notes: Parses the escalation marker, applies the confidence-threshold guardrail, produces the final routable payload.

parameters.query:
insert into retrieval_logs (email_id, email_subject, customer_message, retrieved_chunks, best_score, low_confidence, requires_human, escalation_reason, final_response)
values ($1, $2, $3, $4::jsonb, $5, $6, $7, $8, $9);

nodes.name: Log Retrieval Query
nodes.notes: DAY 4 observability. Runs BEFORE the Gmail action fan-out (Switch Router / Sheets log) so a Gmail-side failure can never wipe out the audit trail. Uses a single-expression array for queryReplacement, not a comma-joined template string - free text containing commas will silently corrupt parameter alignment otherwise (real bug found and fixed during this build).

nodes.name: Switch Router
nodes.notes: Pre-existing routing from the base case. requires_human=true (from either the classifier OR the RAG confidence guardrail) always falls to a human-review branch, never auto-sends.
